maria (DevEx): hey folks — new contributor hitting an odd auth/refresh behavior with the ruby sampleapp when running locally. Token expires and we see 401s, but the SDK doesn't seem to trigger the refresh/retry path. cc @sam

sam (ruby-sdk): thanks for the report. can you share the sampleapp commit + ruby/bundler versions? we shipped a change in 0.6.3 to be friendlier in dev envs, but not sure it covers this case.

maria (DevEx): repro steps i gave them:
1) git clone git@github.com:redwood/sample-ruby.git && git checkout feature/new-onboard
2) bundle install
3) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=short-lived-token
4) ruby bin/sample_echo.rb

After ~30s the app logs:
```
[2026-03-22 15:04:12] ERROR: request failed: 401 Unauthorized
[2026-03-22 15:04:12] INFO: sdk: token expired, checking refresher
[2026-03-22 15:04:12] WARN: sdk: no refresher configured, not retrying
```

We expected the SDK to call the refresh hook and retry once. Running on macOS + Ruby 3.1.2 + bundler 2.4.8.

jyoti (infra): hmm could be the long-lived persistent connection path. The refresher flow was added but only wired to the pooled http client in the hosted flow; local dev uses a short-circuit that missed the hook in some codepaths. We hit a similar CI flake last month.

sam (ruby-sdk): ok that matches a bug i remember. can you try pulling the patch branch?
`bundle add redwood-sdk --version "~> 0.6.3"`
or
`bundle update redwood-sdk && ruby bin/sample_echo.rb`
If you still see it, paste the full log.

maria (DevEx): tried bundle update. logs now show the SDK attempts refresh but fails with an EOF from the refresh endpoint:
```
INFO: sdk: attempting refresh via provided hook
ERROR: refresh failed: EOFError: end of file reached (connection closed)
INFO: sdk: not retrying further, surfacing 401 to app
```
Workaround for now was to set `REDWOOD_DISABLE_LONG_LIVED_CONNECTION=1` which makes the sample app recover and refresh as expected.

sam (ruby-sdk): thanks — that workaround is useful. i'll ask for a small failing spec so we can land a minimal fix. can you open a PR in the ruby-sdk repo with: a) failing test under spec/integration/ that reproduces the EOF/401 path in CI, b) a short patch that ensures the refresher hook runs even when the http pool tears connections? i'll review quickly. :thumbsup:

maria (DevEx): will do. i'll include the sampleapp snippet and CI matrix entry for macOS/ruby-3.1.2. pinging @jyoti for infra eyes on the CI flake.

ci-bot: build queued for PR (ruby-sdk) — runner: macos-12. Logs will appear in ~5m.

jyoti (infra): fyi — if the test needs deterministic refresh responses you can mock the refresh endpoint with mux in the test harness. avoids flaky network.

sam (ruby-sdk): perfect. if you can't get a deterministic repro i can pair to write a tiny unit test that exercises the connection drop path. thanks for catching this — looks like an easy patch once we have the test.

maria (DevEx): opening the PR now: github.com/redwood/ruby-sdk/pull/472 — includes failing spec + suggested fix. i'll add notes about local workaround in the sampleapp README.

sam (ruby-sdk): i'll take first review pass shortly. cheers.
